subject: Post-call: FinLytics discovery — structured outputs, tool-calls, and POC criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Kovacs <ekovacs@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: FinLytics discovery — structured outputs, tool-calls, and POC criteria

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align on a short POC scope.

Key pain points you mentioned
- High per-token cost for live inference on summary and enrichment flows (esp. at 5–10k QPS windows)
- Non-deterministic outputs causing downstream validation failures for automated accounting ingestion
- Multiple internal tools expect strict JSON payloads from the model (transaction records, merchant mapping)

Current stack you shared
- Frontend: React + serverless API on GCP
- Inference today: hosted LLM via generic provider + home-grown post-processing to shape JSON outputs
- Orchestration: Kubernetes for tooling; separate jobs for enrichment and routing

Success criteria for a pilot (as we captured)
1) Deterministic structured outputs: model returns JSON that validates against a schema with >95% pass rate on our sample prompts.
2) Latency: 95th pct < 300ms for single-record enrichment (with batching trade-offs acceptable for bulk jobs).
3) Cost: >=30% reduction in per-token charge or equivalent throughput improvement using quantized/dedicated modes.
4) Integration: tool-calls / function-calling support so model can call your merchant-mapping service (idempotent, authenticated).

Proposed POC scope (2–3 weeks)
- Week 0: Provide sample prompts + 500 gold records (you upload) and a reference JSON schema.
- Week 1: Redwood builds a small inference profile (quantization + batching config), implements a function-call pattern for merchant mapping, and runs 1k test prompts.
- Week 2: Evaluate deterministic pass rate, latency, and cost; iterate on schema/handler edge cases.

Attachments: finlytics-painpoints.pdf (notes), rwi-poc-checklist.xlsx (POC plan), example-schema-sketch.json (template for JSON schema)

Next steps I propose
1) You share the 500 sample records + desired JSON schema by end of next Tue (Nov 24).
2) Ben (cc’d) will schedule a technical deep-dive to validate authentication and network constraints.
3) We’ll confirm POC start date once samples are received — target week of Nov 30.

If that looks right, reply with any changes and I’ll circulate an updated checklist.

Thanks,
—Marissa

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinLytics discovery — structured outputs, tool-calls, and POC criteria

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side:

Clarifications and constraints
- Determinism: our automated accounting pipeline needs the outer JSON structure to be identical for 99% of cases (we can tolerate differences only in a fixed list of optional fields).
- Auth for tool-calls: prefer token-based mutual TLS between Redwood’s function call and our merchant-mapping service. We can provide a short-lived cert or token for the POC.
- Data sensitivity: the sample records will be sanitized (PHI removed), but we need a simple data-retention guarantee for any cached prefixes.

Metrics we’ll track
- Schema pass rate (automated validator you run on Redwood side + our local validator)
- False positive mappings in merchant-mapping (we want precision > 98% on top-1)

We’ll upload the 500 sample records to the Drive link you shared by EOD Monday (Nov 23) and attach a draft JSON schema.

One ask: can your POC include a short smoke test where the model returns a function call instead of inline text when it’s confident about a merchant mapping? That will help our engineers validate the agent workflow.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Kovacs
Head of Product, FinLytics
elena.kovacs@finlytics.com
[Inline: — pasted our short mapping rules for quick reference —]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinLytics discovery — structured outputs, tool-calls, and POC criteria

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications. Short replies inline: 
- Determinism: we’ll run the same prompts under pinned model versions and provide a deterministic-mode run (temperature=0, sampling off) and a structured output validator on our side so you get both the raw model outputs and pass/fail counts.
- Auth: Ben / Aditya will sync on mutual TLS/token flow — Aditya, can you confirm that mutual TLS for a short-lived client cert is supported for the POC?
- Retention: we’ll disable persistent prefix caching for FinLytics data during the POC and add a log-only retention summary.
- Function-calls: yes — we can return structured function-call objects (JSON RPC-like) for confident mappings; we’ll include a fallback inline JSON for uncertain cases.

Action items I’ll take this afternoon
- Attach a first-pass schema sketch (example-schema-sketch.json) with annotations on required fields and enumerations.
- Share a POC checklist updated with mutual TLS steps and the validation procedure.

Ben / Aditya — can you pick a 45-min slot for next Tue or Wed for a technical deep-dive (network + auth + sample throughput)? Prefer slots 9–12 PT.

—Marissa
